title: obdeect versus sim_telarray
reading_guide: **What is compared.** Each case compares obdeect with a reference: an analytic expectation, a sim_telarray, LightEmission or CORSIKA program, or both. Signed values are obdeect / reference − 1, ratios are obdeect / reference, ± is one standard error.

**What PASS means.** All gated checks of the case are inside limits fixed before the run (`details.json`). Where a reference program is known to be wrong, the case is gated against the analytic expectation, and the comparison with that program is *recorded only*: shown, but not part of the verdict.

**Same frame before comparing.** obdeect light sources write photons where they are emitted, the LightEmission programs where they arrive. Before comparing, obdeect photons are moved to the reference plane (flight time added). The time panels show the arrival times as compared.
**Known features of the reference programs.** Some differences in the plots come from the reference, not from obdeect; each affected case has an *Expected differences* box under its figure.
- ff-1m, ff-gct and fake-muon write times in steps of 1/32 ns: their time histograms show spikes or a comb, obdeect times are continuous. Means and widths are compared.

- nsbls samples the photon entry point wrongly (radius `1 − sqrt(u)` instead of `sqrt(u)`, rotated azimuth): its entry-point, time and camera distributions differ from the analytic expectation, which obdeect follows.
- fake-muon times deviate slightly from the analytic distribution; obdeect follows it.

**Image χ²/ndf (chain cases).** Camera images of the same event and telescope from the two runs, pixel by pixel: mean over pixels with signal of (a − b)² / (a + b), with a, b the photoelectrons of the pixel in each run. Differences from Poisson fluctuations alone give about 1; systematic shape differences give more (limit 2). Values below 1 mean the two runs share part of their fluctuations (e.g. identical photons in the stream round trip). For light sources the summed images are compared the same way (χ² per pixel of the normalised images).
**KS.** Largest difference of two cumulative distributions, compared with the critical value for the sample sizes (in brackets where shown).

**Optics.** The star is moved off axis along x (E/W) and along y (N/S). The optics are not rotationally symmetric, so off axis the two directions give different values; each figure shows both, and both programs must agree for each direction.

steps.title: Photon stream format
steps.intro: The obdeect photon stream must carry CORSIKA photons and light-source photons to sim_telarray without loss: CORSIKA → stream → sim_telarray EventIO, compared with sim_telarray on the original CORSIKA file.

steps.title: Atmosphere (propagation)
steps.intro: obdeect propagation (extinction, refraction, travel time) against analytic results, sim_telarray's extinction tables and the compiled CORSIKA atmosphere code.

steps.title: Light sources
steps.intro: obdeect light sources against the sim_telarray LightEmission programs and analytic expectations: photon yield, directions, times and wavelengths at emission, then camera photoelectrons in sim_telarray. Signed values are obdeect / reference − 1; ratios are obdeect / reference.

steps.title: Telescope optics
steps.intro: Ray tracing of obdeect against sim_telarray for the same telescope model, star light at 0–4° off axis along two directions: PSF (D80), effective mirror area and effective focal length.

steps.title: Full chain
steps.intro: obdeect stages inserted into the CORSIKA → sim_telarray chain, compared event by event with the direct sim_telarray run on the same showers and seeds. Bias = obdeect / reference − 1 of camera photoelectrons, with its standard error.

steps.title: Earth curvature (large zenith angles)
steps.intro: At large zenith angles the plane-parallel atmosphere is no longer accurate. obdeect propagation has two curved modes: `spherical` (obdeect applies curvature: emission altitude, extinction and refraction in spherical shells) and `corsika` (CORSIKA with the CURVED option has already curved the shower; obdeect applies the curved extinction only). These cases check the curved geometry and extinction against analytic results and an independent ray tracer, the CURVED flags from CORSIKA through the stream, the mode rules, and CURVED CORSIKA showers at 65° and 75° through obdeect and sim_telarray. sim_telarray itself is plane-parallel, so at these angles it is a reference for the method, not for the result.

steps.title: End-to-end robustness and determinism
steps.intro: Whole-chain properties that do not compare with a reference program: identical output for identical input (threads, chunking, pipes, tee fan-out), rejection of tampered efficiency ledgers, and graceful failure on damaged streams. Pass means zero mismatches and zero silent accepts, with positive controls accepted.

steps.title: Performance
steps.intro: Wall and CPU time of the obdeect chain against sim_telarray on the same input and machine. Informational, no limits.

sources.night-sky.differences: The nsbls curves differ because nsbls is wrong, not obdeect. Projected entry point (top right): an isotropic flux is flat in ρ²; obdeect is flat (KS {projected_area_uniform_native_vs_analytic_ks:.4f}, critical {projected_area_uniform_native_vs_analytic_ks_critical:.4f}), nsbls piles up at the centre (KS {projected_area_uniform_reference_vs_analytic_ks:.2f}) because it draws the radius as 1 − sqrt(u) instead of sqrt(u) and rotates the entry point with the wrong azimuth (`IactLightEmission.cc` ~l.1395). Time (bottom left): the wrong entry points give nsbls a spread of {time_reference_sd_ns:.1f} ns; obdeect has the configured pulse ({time_native_sd_ns:.2f} ns). Camera (bottom right): nsbls puts more light on the dish centre, so its camera sees more; obdeect / nsbls = {camera_pe_ratio:.2f}, recorded only. With the nsbls sampler in obdeect (2026-11-13 report) the camera ratio was 0.998 ± 0.009.
